transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I... well, I hope I'm in the right place. I don't want to be a bother, but I came because I've been feeling just a bit... off, lately. 

I feel terrible even saying it out loud, because I really do have such a wonderful family, but... even when my children come to sit with me, or when the sun is shining right out on my garden—which I usually just love—I just feel so flat inside. It's like the part of me that could be glad, or... or comforted by those nice things, just sort of shut off. 

I hope I'm explaining that okay for you? I know I shouldn't complain when I have so much to be thankful for, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, I suppose it's been... oh, about two weeks now. I really hope I'm not making too much of a fuss over it. I know people go through hard things all the time at my age, and I really should be stronger, but... well, it started right after my husband had a... an emergency. 

He collapsed, you see. Right there in our kitchen. The paramedics had to come in a rush, and they were working on him right there on the floor, and... well, it was just quite a lot to take in. I try not to dwell on it, but that's exactly when this strange feeling started. I'm sorry if I'm rambling, is that the kind of information you need?
Are you still able to enjoy activities or hobbies that you usually found pleasurable before this feeling started?

Well, I suppose that goes back to what I was trying to explain earlier. I hope you don't mind me repeating myself, I know you must be so busy. But yes... things like sitting out in my garden, which I usually just adore, or having my children over. I try to enjoy them, I really do. 

But I just can't seem to feel the joy in them anymore. It's like I mentioned before, I just feel completely flat inside. That little part of me that usually feels glad or gets comforted by those beautiful things... it just feels like it's completely shut off right now. I feel so awful even admitting that out loud, because I really don't want to sound ungrateful for my life. Is that... does that make sense to you, Doctor? I just want to be sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in, even if it's just a little bit?

I... I really wish I could say yes. I feel terrible, I know I should be finding the silver lining. But honestly, no. I've tried, I really have. I'll sit in my favorite chair, or look at the photos of my grandchildren, and I just... I wait to feel that little spark of happiness, but it's just not there. It's just that same flat feeling. I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm being such a downer today. I hope I'm not frustrating you with my answers. I just... I can't seem to find that gladness anywhere right now.
Do you feel guilty about anything in particular?

Guilty? Oh... well, no, I don't think so. I mean, I certainly hope I haven't done anything to feel guilty about. I try very hard to be a good person, you know, to be helpful and not be a burden to anyone. I suppose... well, maybe I feel a tiny bit bad that I'm taking up your time with all my silly feelings, but... no, not guilty about the emergency or anything like that. I know I couldn't have stopped it. I just... I hope I'm being the sort of patient you need me to be. Am I answering that right? I really don't want to make things difficult for you.
Are there any things that you used to look forward to that you no longer look forward to?

Well, yes, I suppose it's just like I was saying a moment ago... I hope you don't mind me bringing it up again. But it's exactly why I decided I needed to come see someone like you. Even when my children come over and sit with me, or when the sun is shining so beautifully on my garden—things I always, always looked forward to—I just feel so terribly flat inside. It's like that piece of me that could be glad or comforted by them just... shut off completely. I hate to keep saying the same thing, I really do. Does that make sense, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you lost interest in activities you usually enjoyed before this feeling started?

Oh, dear... I think I might have just mumbled on about that a second ago, didn't I? I am so sorry if I'm repeating myself, I really don't want to waste your time or sound like a broken record. 

But yes, it's... it's exactly like I was saying about my garden and having my family over. I just don't have that same interest or drive to do those things right now. I know I should, and I feel awful admitting it because I know how blessed I am to have them. I try to keep busy, I really do, but the interest just isn't there. I don't really have any other hobbies or anything new to add, if that's what you mean. 

Did I answer that right, Doctor? I hope I'm being helpful.
Have you been experiencing any changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since you started feeling this way?

Oh... well... no, I don't think so. I mean, I try very hard to eat three meals a day, just like I always have. I know it's important to keep my strength up, especially at my age, so I make sure to have my little bowl of oatmeal in the morning and a sensible dinner. I really don't want to cause any worry for my children by not eating. 

And my sleep... well, I suppose I rest as well as any 81-year-old does, you know? Sometimes I might wake up a little early, but I just lie there quietly so I don't disturb anyone. I certainly wouldn't say there's been any big, dramatic change. I'm doing my best to keep to my normal routine. 

Is that... is that the sort of thing you were asking, Doctor? I hope I'm giving you the right details. I don't want to make a fuss over nothing.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

Well... I wouldn't say sad, exactly. I mean, I know I mentioned feeling a bit flat earlier, but I certainly don't want you to think I'm sitting around crying all day or feeling sorry for myself. I really do try to keep a positive outlook. I know there are people out there with much worse troubles than mine, and I have so much to be thankful for. 

I suppose I just feel a little... empty, maybe? But not a deep sadness. I always try to put on a brave face, especially for my family. I wouldn't want them to think I'm unhappy. I hope that makes sense, Doctor? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can for you.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy that you still find yourself looking forward to, even if you don't end up feeling pleasure from them when you do them?

Oh, goodness... I wish I could give you a better answer for that. I really do. I know I ought to be looking forward to things... like Sunday dinners or my gardening programs. I tell myself I'm going to enjoy them, just like I always did. But... well, if I'm being completely truthful with you—and I know I shouldn't hide things from my doctor—I just don't feel that little spark of anticipation right now. 

I feel terrible even saying it out loud. It makes me sound so ungrateful, doesn't it? I really don't want to be a bother or sound like a complainer. I just sort of go through the motions so I don't let anyone down, but that feeling of looking forward to it just isn't there at the moment. 

I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression, Doctor. Is that the kind of information you needed from me?
Have you been feeling worthless?

Oh, my... no, I wouldn't use a strong word like that. "Worthless" sounds so... so dramatic, doesn't it? I mean, I know I'm 81, and I can't do all the things I used to do when I was younger, but I certainly don't think I'm completely useless. 

I try very hard to still be helpful, you know? I knit little things for the grandchildren, and I always make sure to send a nice card for everyone's birthday. I want to make sure I'm still contributing, even in my own small way. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm just taking up space. 

Sometimes I might feel a little... oh, maybe a bit burdensome to my children, just because I worry about them having to check on me. But I don't feel worthless. I really do try to stay out of their way and not be too much trouble. 

Does that answer your question, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining myself properly. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure most of the day?

Well... I suppose... yes. But I really don't want you to think I'm just being miserable on purpose. I'm so lucky to have my family, and I tell myself that every single day. 

It's just that... well, actually, that's sort of why I came to see you in the first place. It's terribly embarrassing to admit, because it sounds so unappreciative, but... even when my children come over to sit with me, or when it's a beautiful day and the sun is shining right on my garden—things that used to make me so happy—I just feel... flat inside. 

It's almost like... like the part of me that could feel glad about things, or feel comforted by my family being there, has just sort of... shut off. I try so hard to smile for them, I really do, because I don't want to bring them down. 

I feel awful even admitting that out loud. I hope you don't think I'm a terrible person for feeling this way, Doctor? I really am trying my best to appreciate the good things.
Have you been feeling hopeless most of the day?

Oh, hopeless? No, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I know things have been a bit difficult lately, and I've been struggling to feel like myself, but I certainly haven't given up hope. 

I pray every night, you know, and I truly believe things will get better. I have so much faith in the good Lord, and in doctors like you, to help me get back on track. I would never want to sound like I've just thrown in the towel. That wouldn't be very fair to my family, would it? They do so much for me, and I want to be around for them for a long time yet. 

I just... I just want to get back to being the cheerful person they're used to. I'm trying very hard to stay positive, Doctor. I really am. I hope that's the right attitude to have?
Do you feel like you're sad most of the time?

Oh, sad... well, I wouldn't want to use that word exactly. It makes me sound like I'm just sitting around crying all day, and I promise you I'm not doing that. I really do try to keep a brave face on, especially when my family is around. 

I suppose... maybe I feel a bit heavy-hearted sometimes? Just... quiet inside. But I wouldn't call it sadness, not really. I don't want you to think I'm just feeling sorry for myself. There are so many people out there with real problems, and I have a lovely home and a good family. It would be terribly ungrateful of me to just be sad all the time. 

I try to keep busy with my knitting and my little chores, just to keep my mind off things. I hope that's the right way to handle it? I really don't want to be a bother to anyone with my moods.
Do you feel like you're in a low mood most of the day?

Oh, a low mood? Well... I suppose it depends on what you mean by low. I really don't want to come across as a complainer, Doctor. I know I mentioned feeling a bit flat earlier, but I wouldn't say I'm walking around with a dark cloud over my head all day long. 

I mean, I still get up and make my tea, and I always make sure the house is tidy before anyone comes by. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm letting things go. I just... I guess I just don't have that same spring in my step that I used to. 

But I'm sure that's just part of getting older, isn't it? At 81, you can't expect to be doing cartwheels. I try to just take it one day at a time and not dwell on the negative. That's the best way to be, don't you think? I certainly don't want to be one of those sour old ladies who brings everyone down.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you usually enjoyed?

Oh, lost interest? Goodness, no, I wouldn't say that. I still very much enjoy my little routines. Like I mentioned with my knitting, I still make sure to pick it up in the evenings, and I always watch my favorite television programs after supper. 

I suppose... well, maybe I don't knit quite as many squares in a single sitting as I used to, but I certainly haven't lost interest in it. I know it's so important to keep your mind active, isn't it? I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting in my chair staring at the wall all day. That would be a terrible waste of time, and I really do try to stay engaged with the things I've always loved. 

I always make sure to keep myself occupied, Doctor. I hope that shows I'm trying my best to handle everything properly?
Do you feel like your flat mood is mild or more severe?

Oh, well... mild or severe? I suppose... I wouldn't want to use a strong word like severe. It makes it sound like I'm completely falling apart, and I promise you I'm holding things together as best I can. 

But I suppose... well, I did come to see you because... it's just that even when my children come to sit with me, or when the sun is shining so beautifully on my garden—things that have always brought me such joy—I just... I feel so flat inside. It's almost like... like the part of me that could feel glad or find comfort in those things has just... shut off somehow. 

I feel terrible admitting that, because my children are so wonderful to me, and I don't want them to think I don't appreciate them. I really do try to smile and act pleased when they visit. I just... I can't seem to feel it on the inside right now. Is that... is that normal for someone my age going through a difficult patch? I do hope I'm not making too much of a fuss over nothing.
Would you say that this flat feeling inside is something that mildly bothers you or significantly affects your daily life?

Oh, well... significantly affects my life? I wouldn't want to use such a dramatic word. I really do try to manage as best I can, Doctor, I promise I do. 

But... well, I suppose things have changed a little bit lately. I haven't been going down to the senior center like I usually do. I just... I haven't felt quite up to it, and I wouldn't want to bring down the mood for all the other lovely people there. And my daughter, she's such a dear, she's been helping me out a bit more. I feel awful being a burden to her, but... I just haven't been able to keep track of my calendar, or run my little errands. 

She's even been helping with the meals. To be honest with you, I... I mostly just stay in the house now, and I try to avoid the kitchen unless someone is there with me. It just feels a bit overwhelming right now. I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or giving up? I really am trying to push through, but it's just... it's a bit harder to manage things on my own at the moment. Is that alright to admit?
Would you say this feeling of being flat inside is something that mildly bothers you or significantly interferes with your daily activities?

Oh, dear... well, I know you just asked about this, and I don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm complaining... but I suppose it really has been interfering quite a bit. 

I feel so foolish admitting this again, but... yes, I haven't been back to the senior center at all. I just can't seem to muster the energy, and I'd hate to be a wet blanket around my friends there. And... well, I really can't manage my calendar or run my little errands anymore. My daughter has had to step in and do all of that for me. She even manages my meals now. 

I mostly just stay inside the house these days. And... I try to avoid the kitchen entirely unless someone is in there with me. It just feels too much to handle. I know I should be doing better at my age, and I'm so sorry if it sounds like I'm not trying. Do you think it's terrible of me to rely on my daughter so much right now? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something wrong by letting her help me.
Would you say that your flat feeling is something that you can still cope with and manage on most days or is it really impacting your ability to function?

Oh, goodness, I... I know I'm probably repeating myself, and I really don't want to sound like I'm making excuses... but I suppose it truly is impacting my ability to function. 

I'd like to say I'm managing, I really would. But... well, as I mentioned, I just haven't been able to go to the senior center at all. And my poor daughter, she's having to do so much for me—the meals, the errands, keeping track of my calendar. I just stay in the house now, and... and I really can't even bring myself to go into the kitchen unless someone is in there with me. 

I feel so guilty about it, letting her take on all my responsibilities. I should be able to cope better, shouldn't I? I promise I'm not just giving up, it's just... it's all become too much for me to handle on my own right now. Is it okay that I'm letting her do all these things for me? I hope you don't think less of me for it.
